transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Um, I've just been losing a lot of weight recently because I've been barely eating. Most days, I only really manage to eat one or two bites of food. I guess I'm just here because of that.
Do you feel that your eating habits and weight loss are related to concerns about your weight or body shape, or is it more related to a lack of interest in food or feeling full quickly?

It's definitely because I'm terrified of gaining weight or getting fat. The thought of putting on even a single pound makes me incredibly anxious, and I feel like I need to keep losing weight. It's not about a lack of appetite or feeling full; I just can't bring myself to eat because of that fear.
I'm sorry, did you have another question for me? I didn't quite catch what you were about to say.
How do you think you would feel if you were to reach a healthy weight, would that alleviate your fears and anxieties about your body shape, or do you think those feelings would persist?

Honestly, the thought of reaching what you call a 'healthy weight' is absolutely terrifying to me. It wouldn't relieve my anxiety at all; in fact, gaining weight would make my fears and feelings about my body shape so much worse. I just can't handle the idea of getting bigger.
Do you regularly check your weight, or engage in any specific behaviors like excessive exercise, to try to maintain or achieve your desired body shape?
I check my weight on the scale constantly, sometimes multiple times a day. If the number goes up even a tiny bit, I completely panic and feel extremely anxious.
Do you also engage in any rituals or behaviors after eating, such as purging, laxatives, or excessive exercise, to compensate for the calories you've consumed?
No, I don't purge, use laxatives, or do any excessive exercise at all. I simply try to avoid eating and restrict my food intake as much as possible.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'restricting your food intake as much as possible'? How do you decide what you will and won't eat, and are there any specific foods that you completely avoid?

I try to keep my calories as low as possible by eating only a few bites of food a day and often skipping meals entirely. I also strictly avoid carbohydrates and fats because I'm terrified that eating any high-calorie foods will immediately make me gain weight.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms or health problems as a result of your restrictive eating, such as dizziness, hair loss, or difficulty concentrating?

I haven't really noticed any of those physical symptoms like dizziness or hair loss, and I'm not sure about my concentration. My mind is usually just focused on my weight and making sure I don't eat too much.

Based on what you've shared, it sounds like you're experiencing a significant amount of distress related to your eating habits and body image. Would you be open to working with me to develop a treatment plan to address these concerns and improve your overall health and well-being?

I know I'm in a lot of distress, but the idea of a treatment plan is honestly terrifying to me. I'm so scared that getting help means I'll have to gain weight and lose control over my eating habits. It makes it really difficult for me to accept the idea of treatment right now.

I understand that the idea of treatment can be scary, especially when it comes to something as personal as your eating habits and weight. Can you help me understand what you think would need to happen or change for you to feel more comfortable and open to the idea of working together to develop a treatment plan?

I'm really not sure what would need to change to make me feel more comfortable. Right now, the fear of gaining weight is just so overwhelming that it is really hard for me to even think about treatment.
